comment:
* Encapsulates logic to emit notifications to the user that a null cipher is in use. A null cipher * is one that does not attempt to implement any encryption. * *

This class will either emit notifications through SafetyCenterManager if SafetyCenter exists * on a device, or it will emit system notifications otherwise. * * TODO(b/319662115): handle radio availability, no service, SIM removal, etc. * * @hide

methods.name: public void onSecurityAlgorithmUpdate(Context context, int phoneId, int subId, SecurityAlgorithmUpdate update)
methods.comment: * Adds a security algorithm update. If appropriate, this will trigger a user notification.

methods.name: public void setSubscriptionMapping(Context context, int phoneId, int subId)
methods.comment:
* Set or update the current phoneId to subId mapping. When a new subId is mapped to a phoneId,
     * we update the safety source to clear state of the old subId.

methods.name: private void maybeUpdateSubscriptionMapping(Context context, int phoneId, int subId)
public void enable(Context context)
methods.comment:
* Enables null cipher notification; {@code onSecurityAlgorithmUpdate} will start handling
     * security algorithm updates and send notifications to the user when required.

methods.name: public void disable(Context context)
methods.comment:
* Clear all internal state and prevent further notifications until re-enabled. This can be
     * used in response to a user disabling the feature for null cipher notifications. If
     * {@code onSecurityAlgorithmUpdate} is called while in a disabled state, security algorithm
     * updates will be dropped.

methods.name: public boolean isEnabled()
methods.comment: Checks whether the null cipher notification is enabled.

methods.name: private void scheduleOnEnabled(Context context, boolean enabled)
private static boolean shouldIgnoreUpdate(SecurityAlgorithmUpdate update)
methods.comment: Returns whether the update should be dropped and the monitoring state left unchanged.

methods.name: private static boolean isNullCipher(@SecurityAlgorithm int algorithm)
methods.comment:
* Determines whether an algorithm does not attempt to implement any encryption and is therefore * considered a null cipher. * *

Only the algorithms known to be null ciphers are classified as such. Explicitly unknown * algorithms, or algorithms that are unknown by means of values added to newer HALs, are * assumed not to be null ciphers.
